verdict.headline: No trade today
verdict.reason: Still no trade at 6:40am PT. After CAD CPI, USD/CAD broke above 1.4291, pulled back to it, held, and pushed to 1.4303. Price is now 1.4299, stuck in a 4-pip band under 1.4303 resistance, so there's no room to a target. USD/CHF is chopping in a 3-pip band between 0.8397 and 0.8400 with flat EMAs, so it has no break. USD/JPY and GBP/USD are unchanged from the 5:15am plan. No new USD entries until Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 9:00am PT.

watchlist.missing: Long break of 1.4291: the 5:30am CPI candle closed well above it with displacement, and price followed through to about 1.4305 and broke M5 structure. It then pulled back to about 1.4290–1.4293 and held, with bullish candles back up. The EMA 20 (1.4295) is above the EMA 50 (1.4290) with price above both, and RSI is 58 (read on M5). That retest has already played out, though. Price is 1.4299, only 4 pips under 1.4303 resistance, which has rejected twice (wicks to about 1.4306 and 1.4304). Buying here can't reach 1:2. Bodies have closed both sides of 1.4299, so that line isn't a clean break either. New USD entries are blocked until Warsh at 9:00am PT.

Short break of 159.70: there's a close below, follow-through, and a retest to about 159.72 that was rejected with a strong bearish candle. The EMA 20 is below the EMA 50 with price below both, and RSI is 47 (room for a short). M5 isn't in the screenshot, so the structure break is unconfirmed (5/6). The retest entry (about 159.68) has already played out, and price is now 159.51. Selling here with the SL above the retest swing (about 159.76) and TP at 159.34 is under 1:1. US data at 5:30am PT and Warsh at 9:00am PT block it.

Price is 1.3198, between 1.3221 resistance and 1.3183 support, with no break of either. It's sitting on the EMA 20/50 with RSI 53, so there's no direction. A trade needs a displacement close through one level, an M5 structure break and a retest with a candle trigger. The other level is the TP, and the 38-pip range only gives 1:2 with a tight retest stop.

At 6:39am PT, price is 0.8397, sitting on the 0.8397 line just under 0.8400 resistance, which has rejected wicks twice. The overnight drop through both lines (to about 0.8387) didn't hold, and price has ground back up. There's no fresh break: candles have closed on both sides of 0.8397, the EMA 20 (about 0.8396) and EMA 50 (about 0.8395) are flat and tangled with price, and RSI is 54. A short from the 0.8400 rejection fails the EMA check and has no break-and-retest behind it. A long needs a displacement close above 0.8400 and has only 9 pips to 0.8409. C, and new USD entries are blocked until Warsh at 9:00am PT anyway.

newsBlocks: Released: 5:30am PT CAD CPI and US Empire State. USD/CAD broke above 1.4291 on the release. That pair isn't blocked by them any more, but every setup still has to pass the rules.
9:00am PT Fed Chair Warsh speaks: no new entries on any USD pair (all 7 majors) before it. After it, a setup can requalify only if the break-and-retest still holds.
watchFor: USD/CAD (after 9:00am PT): a fresh pullback to 1.4291–1.4293 that holds, with a bullish engulfing or pin bar. Roughly: entry about 1.4292, SL about 1.4287 (2–3 pips under the swing low), TP 1.4303, which is about 1:2.2. Only if RSI is under 70 and the EMA 20 is still above the EMA 50. Or a displacement body close above 1.4303 and a retest from above. Please mark the next resistance above 1.4303 so there's a target to check.
USD/JPY: a fresh pullback to 159.70 that rejects with a bearish engulfing or pin bar and an M5 structure break, with RSI above 30. TP 159.34 gives 1:2+ if the SL is tight above the retest swing.
GBP/USD: a displacement close through 1.3221 or 1.3183, then a retest with a trigger.

USD/CHF (after 9:00am PT): a displacement body close below 0.8397 with the EMA 20 turning under the EMA 50, then a retest from underneath with a bearish engulfing or pin bar. TP 0.8386. Or a strong close above 0.8400 and a retest, but the TP at 0.8409 needs a stop of about 4 pips to make 1:2.

mistakes: None found: no setups were graded or taken, and no entries were made before the 9:00am PT Warsh block. This review covers price action only, not actual OANDA fills. I could only find end-of-day closes and one daily range from same-day market recaps, with no intraday candles, so I can't check whether any watchlist pair broke and retested by the rules after the plan.
lessons: Standing aside looks right. Warsh spoke mostly about AI and gave no hint on rates, so the dollar barely moved after 9:00am PT. Recaps put closes at about USD/CAD 1.4300 (+0.2%), USD/CHF 0.8403 (+0.1%) and USD/JPY 159.48 (-0.2%). USD/CAD ended right under 1.4303 resistance and USD/CHF ended between 0.8400 and 0.8409, which is where they were at plan time. That suggests neither pair made a clean displacement break with room to a 1:2 target, but I can't confirm it without intraday data.

USD/JPY's reported day range was 159.35–159.89. The low stopped about at 159.34 support, so the short from 159.70 would have needed a very tight stop to reach 1:2. The 159.89 high is above the 159.70 retest swing, but I can't tell if it came before or after the plan. If it came after, the short break failed (C).

For tomorrow: USD/CAD is pressing 1.4303, its highest since April 2025. Please mark the next resistance above it so a break can be checked for 1:2. USD/JPY is still capped near 159.90–160.00 with intervention risk. Treat 159.34 as the floor and 159.70 as the line to watch.
review.gradingAudit: No setups were graded. All four watchlist pairs were C, and that holds up on the evidence at plan time: USD/CAD and USD/JPY had retests that had already played out with under 1:2 to target, GBP/USD hadn't broken, and USD/CHF was chopping with flat EMAs. Every USD pair was also blocked until 9:00am PT. The closing prices I found suggest none of them later became a clear A or B, but without intraday candles (fxstreet.com is blocked in this sandbox, and the search results only had closes and a range) I can't rule out a late break and retest.
